concepts.description: A limited-capacity system for temporarily holding and manipulating information during cognitive tasks. In this review it is studied through the Baddeley model.
concepts.name: Working Memory

concepts.description: A multi-component account of working memory that includes a central executive and subsidiary stores such as the phonological loop and visuospatial sketchpad.
concepts.name: Baddeley Model

concepts.description: The relatively permanent storage system for knowledge and experiences, examined here through the encoding, storage, and retrieval framework.
concepts.name: Long-Term Memory

concepts.description: Competing accounts of how attention selects information, including the spotlight model and the zoom lens model.
concepts.name: Theories of Attention

concepts.description: A model describing memory as three stages: encoding information, storing it over time, and retrieving it when needed.
concepts.name: Encoding-Storage-Retrieval Framework

concepts.description: A learning process in which a neutral stimulus becomes associated with a meaningful stimulus, producing a learned response.
concepts.name: Classical Conditioning

concepts.description: A learning process in which behavior is shaped by its consequences, through reinforcement and punishment.
concepts.name: Operant Conditioning

concepts.description: Kahneman's dual-process framework contrasting fast, automatic, intuitive thinking (System 1) with slow, deliberate, effortful reasoning (System 2).
concepts.name: System 1 and System 2 Thinking

concepts.description: Perceptual processing driven by prior knowledge, expectations, and context that shapes how sensory input is interpreted.
concepts.name: Top-Down Perception

concepts.description: Perceptual processing driven by incoming sensory data, building interpretations from the stimulus features upward.
concepts.name: Bottom-Up Perception

concepts.description: A view that attention acts like a beam that enhances processing of whatever falls within its focus, with a fixed or movable size.
concepts.name: Spotlight Model of Attention

concepts.description: A view that attention can vary in size, zooming in for detailed processing of a small area or out for broader coverage with less detail.
concepts.name: Zoom Lens Model of Attention
